title: NLTK ReviewsCorpusReader -- T1499 unbounded FEATURES regex label run causes quadratic backtracking on a bracket-less line
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-12061 (GHSA-fg7f-2386-8897,
CVSS 7.5 HIGH), affecting NLTK's `ReviewsCorpusReader`.

The module-level `FEATURES` regex in `nltk/corpus/reader/reviews.py`
extracts feature annotations (a label followed by a bracketed signed
digit, e.g. `battery life[+1]`) using an unbounded, unanchored label
sub-pattern: a greedy run of word-plus-whitespace groups followed by
a word, which must then be followed by a literal `[`. On a long line
with NO bracket at all, the engine greedily extends the label
candidate from every one of the line's *n* starting positions to the
end of the line, fails to find the bracket, and backtracks the whole
way -- `re.findall` repeating this from every position gives O(n²)
total work. A single crafted bracket-less line of roughly 100,000
words hangs `reviews()`, `features()`, and `sents()` for tens of
seconds to minutes, with no authentication and no privileges
required beyond the ability to supply a reviews corpus the reader
will load.

Detection logic flags a corpus line reachable through
`ReviewsCorpusReader` that exceeds a long word-count threshold with
no `[+N]`/`[-N]` bracketed annotation anywhere in it -- the exact
bracket-less-long-line shape this advisory's proof of concept
measures at O(n²) growth (a 100,000-word line consumes CPU for tens
of seconds to minutes).

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (nltk, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact regex, source file and line numbers,
and a runnable proof of concept comparing vulnerable vs. bounded-fix
growth curves), fixed in NLTK 3.10.0 (PR #3583, verified via live GitHub changelog lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
